chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Abū Jaʿfar, from his father, from Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام, who said:
Nothing spoils the water except that which has flowing blood.

key_terms.الْمَاءَ: water, the subject of the purity ruling
key_terms.سَائِلَةٌ: flowing, meaning blood that gushes or runs when cut
key_terms.نَفْسٌ: a living soul, used here in the technical sense of possessing blood
key_terms.يُفْسِدُ: renders corrupt or impure in the legal sense

ai.seo_question: What kinds of dead creatures make water impure in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning ritual purity: water is not rendered impure by the death of a creature in it unless that creature possesses flowing blood. It is a foundational text in Shia fiqh for distinguishing between animals whose carcasses affect water and those that do not.
